The word caldera, as far as I can tell, shares its root with cauldron. These are large bowl shaped depressions that are left after a massive volcanic eruption.

Like all volcanoes, calderas have a magma chamber that feeds the volcano. For calderas though these magma chambers can be yuuuuge. They are the best magma chambers, like none you've ever seen. Believe me, I know.

Calderas can form from both effusive eruptions (the shield volcano type), and explosive eruptions (the stratovolcano type). The type of lava isn't important for the formation of calderas. What is important is that enough magma is emptied from the magma chamber that the volcano collapses in on itself. It's like a volcanic sink hole (more on sink holes in a later post).

The caldera crater generally has a circular, stair case shape leading down towards the center. This cross section of Rotorua in New Zeland shows the stair case pattern fairly well. https://images.duckduckgo.com/iu/?u=http%3A%2F%2Fvolcano.oregonstate.edu%2Fvwdocs%2Fvolc_images%2Faustralia%2Fnew_zealand%2FNZ23.jpg&f=1 The gray rock is from lava flows that have hardened. The green is the country (basement) rock, and the two ignimbrite (old pyroclastic flows) layers show the stair step pattern caused by the magma chamber collapse.

The two types of magmas (felsic and mafic) tend to form calderas very differently. Mafic magmas (effusive, shield volcano types) tend to empty the magma chamber out over a long period of time, over which the caldera forms slowly. Kilauea will probably turn into a caldera as it moves off of the hotspot under Hawaii. Felsic magmas (explosive type eruptions - think Yellowstone) have very violent eruptions during which the magma chamber collapses quickly. When Yellowstone goes off it is going to be a very bad day for the Western US, and a pretty bad day for the Eastern US as well.

I use Pale Moon for now. It's an open source fork of Firefox that removes a bunch of (pretty much useless) features. It's lighter, faster, and crashes less. It is able to use Firefox add-ons (although not all of them are compatible). I used to use NoScript, HTTPSEverywhere and PrivacyBadger. But the latter two are now incompatible with Pale Moon (because firefox have changed their API) so I've switched to using HTTPNowhere (and the only real reason to use Privacy Badger is to have a fallback layer so you can just "allow all this page temporarily" in NoScript from time to time)

Also Tor Browser Bundle for anything the current government or any future government might be interested in i.e. media, anonymous messaging boards, dodgy links you come across, etc.
